paper.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning

result.summary: 本文挑战了大型语言模型复杂推理需要海量训练数据的假设，提出 Less-Is-More Reasoning (LIMO) 假说 [S3.p1]。作者通过多层筛选构建了仅 800 条样本的 LIMO 数据集，并在 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 上做简单监督微调 [S1.p4]。LIMO 在 AIME24 上达到 63.3%、MATH500 上达到 95.6%，超过此前微调模型且仅用其 1% 的训练数据 [abstract]。作者认为，在预训练已编码领域知识的基础模型中，复杂推理可通过少量但精心设计的认知过程演示被激发 [S3.p1]。

research_question.text: 本文要解决的问题是：大型语言模型的复杂推理是否必须依赖海量训练数据，还是可以通过极少量高质量示例来激发 [abstract]。原文指出，此前关于推理任务的数据效率研究仍使用远多于 LIMA 的数据量，能否将质量优先的思路应用于推理任务尚不确定 [S2.SS3.p1]。

evidence.quote: We challenge the prevailing assumption that complex reasoning in large language models (LLMs) necessitates massive training data.
However, whether this lesson can be applied to reasoning tasks remains uncertain, given the potential high computational complexity of such tasks.
the quantity of such data is still much larger compared to that in LIMA

method.text: 作者提出 LIMO 假说：在预训练已全面编码领域知识的基础模型中，复杂推理能力可通过少量但精确编排的认知过程演示而涌现 [S3.p1]。基于此，作者设计多层数据筛选流程，从大量问答对中先做粗粒度难度过滤、再做细粒度难度评估和知识点多样化，同时按逻辑连贯性、步骤清晰度和解答正确性筛选推理链，最终得到 800 条训练样本 [S1.p4]。然后使用该数据集对 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 进行简单监督微调 [S1.p4]。

evidence.quote: sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through minimal but precisely orchestrated demonstrations of cognitive processes
first conducting coarse difficulty filtering to eliminate trivial problems, then fine-grained difficulty assessment to identify challenging questions, followed by knowledge point diversification
we filter reasoning chains based on logical coherence, step-by-step clarity, and solution accuracy
This meticulous process yields a compact yet potent dataset of just 800 training samples.
With simple supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using only this curated dataset based on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct

experiments.text: 实验在数学推理基准上进行，包括 AIME24 和 MATH500 [abstract]。作者将 LIMO 与先前微调模型比较，并对比了更大规模数据集 NuminaMath-100k 和 OpenThoughts-114k [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1]。此外，作者通过控制实验比较同一问题不同质量推理链的效果 [S6.SS3.SSS1.p1]，并比较不同预训练基础模型（Qwen2.5 与 Qwen1.5）的影响 [S6.SS3.SSS3.p2]。

evidence.quote: achieves 63.3% accuracy on AIME24 and 95.6% on MATH500
NuminaMath-100k shows significant degradation (32.3% vs. base model’s 49.9%)
We investigate what characteristics define superior reasoning chains that lead to better model performance through a controlled comparative study
LIMO (built on Qwen2.5) achieves 63.3% accuracy on AIME2024, a 54.1 percentage point improvement over Qwen1.5’s 9.2%.

findings.text: LIMO 在 AIME24 上达到 63.3%、MATH500 上达到 95.6%，超过此前微调模型（AIME24 6.5%、MATH500 59.2%），且仅使用其 1% 的训练数据 [abstract]。在分布外泛化上，LIMO 取得 45.8% 的绝对提升，优于用 100 倍数据训练的模型 [abstract]。对比实验中，LIMO 的 800 条精选问题达到 78.1%，优于 NuminaMath-100k 的 32.3% 和 OpenThoughts-114k 的 58.3% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1]。预训练基础模型影响显著：基于 Qwen2.5 的 LIMO 在 AIME2024 上比基于 Qwen1.5 的高 54.1 个百分点，在 MATH500 上高 30.4 个百分点 [S6.SS3.SSS3.p2]。

evidence.quote: achieves 63.3% accuracy on AIME24 and 95.6% on MATH500, surpassing previous fine-tuned models (6.5% on AIME24, 59.2% on MATH500)
while using only 1% of the training data required by prior approaches
achieving a 45.8% absolute improvement across diverse benchmarks, outperforming models trained on 100× more data
LIMO’s carefully curated 800 problems yield superior performance (78.1%)
a 54.1 percentage point improvement over Qwen1.5’s 9.2%
On MATH500, LIMO reaches 95.6% accuracy, surpassing Qwen1.5 by 30.4 percentage points.
